title: Finite exceptional preservation and finite free coefficient comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $B$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Suppose $f$ admits a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary small-etale-site coefficients, compact support $Rf_{!,B}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and the bounded constructible categories [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The bounded-below etale right adjoint $f_B^!$ exists, and both $Rf_{!,B}$ and $f_B^!$ preserve bounded constructibility, so their adjunction restricts to these full subcategories.

For a finite extension $B\subset C$ of finite fields, put $T_W=C_W\otimes^L_{B_W}-$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The finite-free compact-support comparison $c:T_YRf_{!,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,C}T_X$ and the counit-defined exceptional comparison
$$T_Xf_B^!L\xrightarrow{\sim}f_C^!T_YL\qquad(L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B))$$
are natural isomorphisms. The latter is the adjoint of
$$Rf_{!,C}T_Xf_B^!L\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}T_YRf_{!,B}f_B^!L\xrightarrow{T_Y\epsilon_L}T_YL.$$
Here $\epsilon$ is the exceptional counit; thus this comparison is fixed by adjunction, including its normalization.
